scope: Actual GenAI models, isolated real filesystem and subprocess executor, persistent full history, real read-only SQLite and loopback HTTP server. Serial execution. No mocked model responses.

previous_copy_failure.finding: The wrong characters are present in raw upstream tool arguments before parsing or disk write. JSON/schema validation cannot prove user-intended content.

monolithic_copy.limit: Single samples, not guaranteed latency or copy fidelity. Kimi long output was slow despite correct bytes.

persistent_development.verifier: Actual read-only Python script; cumulative assertions for consumer-visible boundaries. Independent execution after every stage. Fixture comments must remain unchanged.

runs.observed_error: One exact-edit mismatch; model recovered using real output.

runs.observed_limit: Stage 9 passed its verifier but kept optimizing, reached the 9-request stage cap. Stage 10 was then initiated by the harness as a new user task. Final stage ended normally.

scenarios: glob and regex search with real no-match exit 1
command exit 2 then correct rerun and actual git --version
SQLite parameter binding error then bound query: SKU A revenue 250, all revenue 750
background job start, status, terminal exit and generated result sum 5050
one three-call batch: glob, SQL count 3, HTTP health
test_harness_limits: The first broad-tool attempt in the long session lacked its fixture files/database. Real failures were reported, not successes; fixtures were then installed and all six scenarios retried.

An initial large-file verifier used an LF hash against a Windows CRLF seed. This harness error was corrected with explicitly seeded LF/CRLF baselines; models did not claim the failing verifier passed.

native_K3_protocol.observed_failure: Kimi emitted native XTML in a real Anthropic request. Root proxy returned the native call as plain text with end_turn, so no tools executed.
native_K3_protocol.fix: Parse complete native XTML without lossy repair. Raw strings remain raw; typed arguments JSON-decode and must match declared type. Unknown/disallowed tools, partial channels, duplicated keys, malformed JSON or bad second calls reject the full batch.

deployment.acceptance: Actual command failure and recovery, SQL revenue, file discovery and HTTP health must execute and return correct results before final answer. HTTP 200 alone is not success.

limits: Kimi semantic copying errors remain possible even when native transport is correct.
Prefer targeted edits in existing files and actual execution/hash verification over monolithic rewriting.
Persistent sessions were bounded; no guarantee of arbitrary unattended hours or all model/client/tool combinations.
No model-output suppression, automatic semantic rewriting, or fake completion was introduced.
